findings.title: Active Members summary card total disagrees with per-team breakdown on same dashboard
findings.description: On the usage dashboard's 'Meridian Health — June' view, the headline 'active members' summary card shows 280 for the month while the per-team breakdown directly below it sums to 412, matching the admin panel's true count. The two numbers were in agreement until roughly a week to a week and a half before the call. The customer uses this card to report adoption numbers to finance, and last month a VP asked why adoption 'fell off a cliff' when the underlying number had actually risen. The customer will send a screenshot showing the card and breakdown together in the same frame.
findings.quote: The headline "active members" card — the big number at the top — says 280 for this month. Our admin panel says 412.
findings.severity_reason: Wrong headline metric is feeding a customer's finance/ops reporting and directly undermines the renewal narrative, even though the underlying detailed data is correct.
findings.match_note: No catalogue issue covers a dashboard summary-card vs. breakdown data mismatch; distinct from the timezone display issue (PROJ-101).

findings.title: Scheduled report timestamps off by several hours (timezone handling)
findings.description: Customer reports that since May, scheduled report timestamps appear off by a few hours. Customer confirms BetterBark support already identified this as the known timezone issue and that Meridian Health is on the list for the fix; they are only reconfirming it is still occurring, not re-reporting it as new.
findings.quote: back in May we saw the report timestamps looking off by a few hours. But your team already told us that's the known timezone thing
findings.severity_reason: Confirmed still-present instance of an already-tracked, in-progress defect; no new scope or symptom, customer is not blocked and is aware a fix is coming.
findings.match_note: Same symptom (report timestamps off) and same account (Meridian Health) as PROJ-101, which the customer explicitly confirms is the known, already-attached issue.

findings.title: Dashboard team-label font size hard to read on laptop
findings.description: Customer asks if the small gray team labels under the summary card could be a notch bigger, since they squint at them on a laptop screen. Customer explicitly frames this as nitpicking, attributes it to their own eyesight/laptop rather than a product defect, and tells the CSM not to file it.
findings.quote: could the dashboard font be a notch bigger? I'm on a laptop screen half the day and I squint at the little team labels under the card.
findings.severity_reason: Purely cosmetic preference explicitly retracted by the customer as not a real complaint.
findings.match_note: No catalogue match; excluded per rule that self-described 'not a real complaint' taste remarks are not filed.

findings.title: Social awkwardness reported when members request a trainer switch
findings.description: Customer relays that a few members asked whether they can switch trainers without it feeling like 'a breakup,' describing social awkwardness around re-matching. No product defect or feature gap is identified; the CSM characterizes it as a program-design/communications issue and offers to send comms language rather than a product change, and no product change is requested.
findings.quote: a few people asked whether they can switch trainers without it feeling like a breakup. There's some social awkwardness to it.
findings.severity_reason: Not a product defect or capability gap; addressed via customer communications, not engineering.
findings.match_note: No catalogue issue applies; this is a program-design/comms concern, not a product bug or feature request.
